title: Exploring napping paradigm for Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2609.13927v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Biological organisms minimize free energy by balancing two competing demands on their internal world model: it must be accurate enough to predict sensory input, yet simple enough to generalize beyond it. Two mechanisms regulate this balance offline: sleep reduces complexity through gradual synaptic downscaling, while stochastic noise attenuates precision, relaxing the constraint sensory input imposes on synaptic reorganization. Engineered Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) leave this balance unaddressed, favoring instantaneous, noiseless weight normalization instead. This paper investigates the hypothesis that a biologically inspired micro-sleep paradigm, napping -- combining proportional weight scaling with continuous stochastic membrane activity -- can replicate the stability of normalization while shedding model complexity. We evaluate this in an unsupervised recurrent SNN trained via trace-based spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) o

translated_title: 探索循环脉冲神经网络的“小睡”范式
translated_abstract: 生物有机体通过平衡其内部世界模型所面临的两种相互竞争的需求来最小化自由能：该模型必须足够精确以预测感觉输入，同时又必须足够简单以便在输入之外实现泛化。有两种机制在离线状态下调节这一平衡：睡眠通过逐渐的突触缩减来降低复杂度，而随机噪声则衰减精度，从而放松感觉输入对突触重组所施加的约束。工程化的脉冲神经网络（SNN）并未解决这种平衡问题，而是倾向于采用即时的、无噪声的权重归一化。本文研究了这样一个假设：一种受生物学启发的微睡眠范式——“小睡”，即将比例权重缩放与连续的随机膜活动相结合——能够在降低模型复杂度的同时复制归一化的稳定性。我们在一个通过基于痕迹的脉冲时序依赖可塑性（STDP）训练的无监督循环SNN中对此进行了评估。
tldr: 本文提出一种受生物学启发的“小睡”范式，将比例权重缩放与随机膜活动相结合，使无监督循环脉冲神经网络在降低模型复杂度的同时获得与权重归一化相当的稳定性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a biologically inspired "napping" paradigm—combining proportional weight scaling with stochastic membrane activity—that enables unsupervised recurrent spiking neural networks to achieve stability comparable to weight normalization while reducing model complexity.
